entities.summary:
Alibaba Group Holding Limited is a Chinese multinational technology company founded by Jack Ma and 17 co-founders in 1999 in Hangzhou, China. It became the world's largest retail commerce company by gross merchandise volume, pioneering e-commerce and cloud computing across Asia and emerging markets.

Alibaba's Taobao and Tmall platforms created China's dominant e-commerce ecosystem, processing more transactions on Singles' Day (November 11) than the combined annual revenue of many Fortune 500 companies. Alipay, its payment platform, revolutionized digital payments in China and became one of the world's largest financial technology platforms, now operating under Ant Group. AliCloud became Asia's leading cloud computing provider, competing with AWS and Azure globally.

Alibaba's growth enabled tens of millions of small businesses in China and Southeast Asia to participate in global commerce, lifting many entrepreneurs from poverty. The company's 2014 IPO on the New York Stock Exchange raised $25 billion, the largest IPO in history at that time. However, Jack Ma's regulatory conflicts with Chinese authorities from 2020 onward demonstrated the tensions between private tech giants and state power in authoritarian systems.
